messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@caleidohealth.com>, Michael Tran <michael.tran@caleidohealth.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com, aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: token economics & batching assumptions — Caleido Health

Hi Sarah / Michael,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the clear breakdown of your primary use cases (clinical note summarization, intake form normalization, and an in-app assistant). Per our discovery I wanted to put the key pricing/technical assumptions in one place so procurement has something concrete to evaluate: 

Summary of your info (confirm if anything below is off):
- Estimated steady-state traffic: 40M–60M tokens/month (range driven by adoption scenarios).
- Workload mix: 60% short-callouts (prompts + short responses, ~150 tokens total), 30% medium summaries (~700 tokens total), 10% long transcripts (~2k tokens).
- Concurrency profile: spikes up to ~18 concurrent interactive users during clinic hours, baseline concurrency ~6.
- SLA target: <250ms p95 for short-callouts; willing to accept 400–500ms for heavy summaries.
- Budget guidance: procurement indicated target unit economics of ~$10–$18 / 1M tokens (ballpark).

Redwood assumptions and preliminary proposal items (for discussion):
- Continuous batching: based on the short/medium split and your concurrency, we estimate an effective batching factor of ~5–7 for interactive short-callouts (higher for batch summary jobs). That assumes continuous dispatching with a 50–80ms batching window tuned to meet your p95 target.
- KV/prefix cache reuse: for note-followups we expect ~40–60% cache reuse, lowering effective compute by ~0.4x on those flows.
- Token unit pricing: host proposal range $9–$16 / 1M tokens depending on commitment tier and whether you choose dedicated pools. (Dedicated capacity lowers unit cost but requires commit.)
- Burst and headroom: with your 18-concurrency spikes we recommend a config that autos-scales with 30–40% headroom; for strict latency SLOs we'd recommend enabling short-path low-latency nodes (slightly higher unit cost) for the <250ms tier.

Requested confirmation / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the 40M–60M tokens/mo range or provide a best guess for Q3?
2) Which endpoint latency tier matters most for billing: strict (<250ms) vs relaxed (400–500ms)?
3) Will summaries/transcripts be run as background batch jobs (can tolerate higher queueing) or interactive?

I attached a one-page mutual action plan (MAP_v1.pdf) + a draft SOW for your legal team to start review. If values above look reasonable I can run a cost model and a couple of pricing options (hosted, reserved/dedicated, and mixed routing) and send them back by Thursday.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0133

Subject: Re: Follow-up: token economics & batching assumptions — Caleido Health

Hi Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. A few confirmations and clarifications below: 

Confirmations:
- Tokens: 45M/month looks like the realistic baseline for our pilot (clinics A+B). If pilot adoption hits our optimistic case we could see 75M/mo across the org.
- Concurrency: the 18 user spike is correct for peak clinic hours; off-hours drop to 2–3 concurrent users.
- Summaries: long transcripts will be background jobs submitted nightly (non-interactive). The in-app assistant and intake normalizer are interactive and need the lower-latency tier.

Budget note from procurement (procurement@caleidohealth.com):
- Our CFO carved out $60k/mo for pilot inference spend; for procurement acceptance we need a credible plan that lands ~ $12–$16 / 1M tokens (pilot), and lower if we commit longer term.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) If we target $14 / 1M tokens for the pilot (45M/mo), what does the hosted vs dedicated pricing look like monthly? Can you show a blended $/1M based on mixed routing (interactive on low-latency reserved nodes + summary jobs on hosted cheaper nodes)?
2) What continuous batching latency knobs would you enable to meet 250ms p95 for 150-token exchanges at our concurrency? Any chance you can share a small A/B table that shows batching window vs p95 latency vs cost estimate?

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps.

—Sarah
Sarah Lewis
Head of Product | Caleido Health
sarah.lewis@caleidohealth.com | +1 617-555-0199
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: quick pricing sketch for Caleido (notes)

Vanessa — copying quick sketch for the cost model you promised to run. Use these when you reply: 

Assumptions (normalize to 45M tokens/mo pilot):
- Mix: 60% interactive short (150 tokens), 30% medium (700 tokens), 10% batch long (2k tokens).
- Effective batching factor (interactive): 6 -> reduces per-token GPU time by ~1/6 vs no-batching; batch long jobs see factor 12+.
- Cache reuse: 0.5 average across flows -> ~20% fewer new tokens to compute.

Pricing options (ballpark):
- Hosted (no commit): $16 / 1M tokens (baseline), expected monthly = $720 (per 45M/1M * $16 = $720) — wait arithmetic check: actually 45 * $16 = $720.
- Mixed routing (reserved low-latency nodes for interactive + hosted for batch): blended $/1M ≈ $13–$14 depending on reserved commitment and autoscale config.
- Dedicated (1yr commit/reserved capacity): $9–$11 / 1M tokens (with SLA and priority routing).

Notes on continuous batching knobs to include in the A/B table for Sarah:
- Batching window (ms): 20 | 50 | 100 -> p95 approx: 180ms | 230ms | 320ms (for 150-token exchange at concurrency 8–12). Cost impact: smaller window -> fewer tokens batched -> ~7–20% higher CPU/GPU cost.
- Target concurrency for low-latency pool: 12 concurrent workers with 30% headroom for spikes -> keeps p95 under 250ms at 150-token prompts.

I'll pull a quick cost spreadsheet and a two-option deck (pilot hosted+reserved vs dedicated pilot) — ping me if you want me on the call with Caleido.

—Sean
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: token economics & batching assumptions — Caleido Health

Sarah / procurement team — thanks for the confirm. Per Sean's sketch above I've attached the MAP and a two-option pricing snapshot:

Option A — Mixed routing (recommended for pilot):
- Reserved low-latency pool sized for interactive traffic during peak hours (enough to handle 12 concurrent workers + 30% headroom).
- Background/summary jobs routed to standard hosted endpoints.
- Blended pilot price target: $13.75 / 1M tokens -> Estimated monthly cost at 45M = $618.75.
- Pros: keeps interactive p95 <250ms; no 1yr commitment; can convert to dedicated later.

Option B — Short-term dedicated commit (12 months, discount):
- 12mo reserved capacity with priority routing and SLA.
- Pilot blended price target: $10.50 / 1M tokens -> Estimated monthly at 45M = $472.50.
- Tradeoffs: commit required; better predictable unit economics.

Attached: MAP_v1.pdf (action items + owners), SOW_draft.docx (scope + timeline), cost_snapshot.xlsx (pricing table), and network_diagram.png.

Requested next steps:
- Procurement: please confirm which option you prefer to see a final quote (A vs B) and whether you need a signed NDA/PO first.
- Sarah: if you'd like, Sean and I can run a 15–20 minute micro-demo of the interactive 150-token flow so you can observe p95 with batching window toggles live.

If I don't hear back, I'll follow up next Wednesday with the formal two-option quote + HubSpot deal update.

Thanks again — excited to keep this moving.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
